### A Prayer to Obey When Faced with Temptations
Author: Chelsey DeMatteis
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-prayer/a-prayer-to-obey-when-faced-with-temptations.html
Passage: Joshua 7:11
Points:
- Disobedience and hidden sin at Jericho resulted in Israel's unexpected defeat and dismay at Ai.
- God’s commands are holy boundaries rather than optional suggestions, and violating them brings consequences.
- Like Achan, people often choose secret defiance, only to see life unravel when truth surfaces.
- Concealed sin never stays isolated; it ripples outward to wound families and communities.
- Bringing hidden sins into God's light leads to freedom and redemption through Christ.

### A Time to Wait in Prayer
Author: Charles F. Stanley
Site: In Touch Ministries
URL: https://www.intouch.org/read/daily-devotions/a-time-to-wait-in-prayer
Passage: Joshua 7:1-13
Points:
- Israel's retreat and loss of thirty-six soldiers stemmed from both hidden sin and self-directed action.
- Joshua listened to human advisors and failed to seek heavenly guidance before attacking Ai.
- Facing difficult challenges in our own strength inevitably invites failure.
- Unaddressed sin skews human judgment and disrupts open communication with God.
- Believers must honestly examine their hearts, confess wrongdoing, and patiently wait for God's direction.

### The Seriousness of Sin
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/seriousness-sin/
Passage: Joshua 7:1
Points:
- Israel's downfall at Ai demonstrated the heavy cost of breaking covenant faithfulness with the Lord.
- Achan’s private theft of devoted Jericho spoils brought corporate consequence upon all of Israel.
- God required the dedicated items and the transgression to be removed to protect the camp's purity.
- Achan only confessed after being singled out by God, demonstrating fear rather than heartfelt repentance.
- While God extends mercy to the truly penitent, unrepentant defiance ultimately meets condemnation.

### Bible Pathway - Mar. 15, 2011
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-mar-15-2011.html
Passage: Joshua 7:1
Points:
- Riding high after Jericho, Israel assumed continued victory without inquiring of the Lord.
- Joshua and his scouts devised their own strategy instead of waiting for God's explicit commands.
- The army engaged in battle unaware that God's presence and favor were no longer with them.
- Activity in God's service cannot substitute for seeking His guidance in humble prayer.
- The failure at Ai illustrates that apart from the Lord, human effort accomplishes nothing.
